sermon.title: Obtaining the Promises - July 23, 2023
sermon.speaker: Michael Silla
sermon.summary: God’s promises—forgiveness, the Holy Spirit, eternal life, a new heaven and earth—are for all. Abraham was fully convinced and acted; Jonathan believed but didn’t make the transition. The woman with the flow of blood, the Canaanite woman, the sinful woman and the centurion show humble faith that obtains the promises, and Christ has power to perform them.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then Peter said to them, “Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is to you and to your children, and to all who are afar off, as many as the Lord our God will call.”

Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right. “Honor your father and mother,” which is the first commandment with promise: “that it may be well with you and you may live long on the earth.”
And this is the promise that He has promised us—eternal life.
Behold, I send the Promise of My Father upon you; but tarry in the city of Jerusalem until you are endued with power from on high.”
Nevertheless we, according to His promise, look for new heavens and a new earth in which righteousness dwells.
